scope: Read-only installed SDK/source inspection and frozen server/application log correlation. No code changes, tests, services or inferred remediation.

summary.interpretation: Server job failure and application cleanup/worker exit are separate observations. SDK source places room departure before registered application callbacks and before eventual JS_SUCCESS construction; all four logs are consistent with that ordering. The server error text does not come from Python _update_job_status, which always sends an empty error field.

source_evidence.observation: Lifecycle handler asynchronously schedules _update_job_status and owns its task.
Status reporting is registered for process_started, process_closed and process_job_launched.
Executor SUCCESS maps to JS_SUCCESS, FAILED to JS_FAILED; UpdateJobStatus always has error="", then queues the message.

supported_inference: A departure-versus-final-status ordering mismatch is a concrete hypothesis: the server records agent departure as failure before the SDK reaches its post-join success reporting path.

PRISM invokes the SDK shutdown API from the close event; no separate PRISM room.disconnect or manual failed-status assignment exists in that bridge. A defect in our callback order is not established by these labels.
The same label occurs in8/8 iteration7,4/4 iteration8 and4/4 iteration9 records, so it predates the iteration9 ETA/request-fidelity changes.
limits: We did not capture outgoing worker UpdateJobStatus frames or a server status-transition history. Source shows when the SDK would construct success, not that success was sent, received, accepted or persisted for these specific jobs.

The running server source at agent/worker.go:556 and the server branch that creates agent worker left the room were not inspected. We cannot establish whether this label is expected policy, terminal state winning a race, an SDK/server compatibility issue, or a reporting defect.
Do not call the server failures harmless or remediated. Application cleanup, agent absence, known navigation effects and process exit0 do not prove server JS_SUCCESS.
Thread executor SUCCESS is assigned after normal join in the inspected code; worker process exit0 is weaker than independently observed per-job status success.

Only worker.py and job_thread_executor.py among these SDK sources are directly frozen by the worker launch receipt; additional SDK files are exact current local sources with their hashes, not new runtime instrumentation.

Server timestamps are millisecond precision with +0530 offset; application timestamps are UTC with microseconds. Differences are wall-clock log correlations on the same host, not exact wire latency or proof of message-processing order.
